source.value:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$

source.value:
We know that any vector in  $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \}$ has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $x_1$ and $x_2$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,\mathcal{B}.$ Since we are told that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065173/assets/93ae6d0ad6dbd6036c99e5d2fcb55789fef9b2e576300f13b43ed561856fa218.png) we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(-1)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

source.question: e-4824
source.value:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -11 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065173/assets/14c42b3d306468a8a17f5ffaef535dd39c6d5fdb079366d9f495774b6e019815.png)

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 \\ 3 & 5 & -11 \\ 4 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 4 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & -12 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The augmented matrix above corresponds to the following system of equations: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=-5 \\ -4{x}_{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $x_2 =-1.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1 + 3 \left( -1 \right)  = -5
\qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad
x_1 = -2.
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065173/assets/5e92e3cfdbf8d1c81be5b47124df9992d98835668154a50ece28cce8941860ca.png)

source.question: e-4825
source.value:
We need to find $x_1,$ $x_2,$ and $x_3$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above system as an augmented matrix $M$ and reducing using Gaussian elimination, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -9 & -1 & 7 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -9 & -1 & 7 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -9 & -1 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{4}{3} & \frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=1 \\ -9{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=7 \\ \frac{4}{3}{x}_{3}=\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3 =2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
-9x_2 - 2 = 7 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 = -1,
$$

and substituting $x_2=-1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x_1+3(-1) = 1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1 = 4.
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065173/assets/61d8401f40152a8eaeb30d3dc55d9548cac508b6239a9a70e99fbed9e271805b.png)
